label: Every actual root is constitutively simple: at most one real constituent
paraphrase: OPEN analyst reading of commitment (a) of #2145, attribution deferred: for every actual concrete root r at w, any two real constituents of r are identical, so r has at most one real constituent. A real constituent is something in r with being in reality as a part, principle, property or aspect of r, not merely an object of apprehension or a term of a relation of reason. Non-real items (objects of understanding, modes, distinctions of reason) are not counted, so the premise does not by itself deny a plurality of such items in r. The personal account and the noncognitive imitability-exemplar rival (A4) both grant it; it is the simplicity both describe as a simple nature.
